study_identification_part.si4_title: Dynamic gray matter volume changes in pediatric multiple sclerosis: A 3.5 year MRI study

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Linear models were used to estimate correlations between GM volume z-scores and clinical/lesional variables (disease duration, EDSS, IQ, T2/T1 LV). Linear models were also used to assess the correlation between changes in z-scores and baseline IQ and changes in LV.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Impaired gray matter maturation occurs in pediatric MS patients, contributing to disability independently of white matter inflammation, while high IQ may offer protection.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Pediatric MS patients showed widespread failure of GM development and progressive atrophy, particularly in cortical and deep GM regions, which was only partially related to WM lesions. Higher disability (EDSS) correlated with more severe atrophy in the thalamus and caudate. Higher IQ was associated with less GM deviation at baseline and slower atrophy progression over 3.5 years. Some brain regions also showed a reduction in deviation over time, suggesting potential plasticity or reparative mechanisms.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Only a subset of patients had longitudinal follow-up; IQ was the only measure of reserve analyzed; clinical stability of the cohort limited the ability to predict disability worsening.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: This study is not without limitations. First, only part of our patients underwent a clinical and MRI follow-up assessment...Second, we analyzed only IQ as a possible measure of reserve...Finally, the clinical stability of our patients during the study period did not allow any analysis of prediction of disability worsening.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study highlights the importance of using a large external control dataset (NIH HC) to model developmental trajectories when longitudinal pediatric control data is scarce. It also demonstrates a voxel-wise approach to track deviations from these norms over time.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: The study found that magnetic field strength (MFS) had a significantly smaller effect on GM volume estimates compared to age and sex, but it was still included as a covariate to handle potential bias between scanners.
